issues: Sheets 05-13: the 'pink' is never pink. The flash where the drop lands is a mustard-yellow ellipse and the endpoint fill is olive/khaki; the one visual fact the clip exists to teach (faint pink that lasts) is shown in the wrong color, actively mis-teaching what to look for

Sheets 01-13: the apparatus is a small thin-line burette and flask pinned mid-frame occupying maybe a quarter of the 9:16 canvas; the bottom third is empty chalkboard and the flask (where all the action happens) is tiny, so drops and the color change are hard to see on a phone

Sheets 06-10: the flash/fade/linger cycle reads as the same blob appearing and dimming; there is no visible difference between 'flashes then fades' and 'starts to linger', no swirl motion, and no visible slowing of drop rate for 'drop by drop', so motion does not carry the narration's meaning

Sheets 01-13: captions are small, light-weight and chopped into 2-3 word fragments ('with a', 'Stop at a', 'Then read the') that flip every half second and sometimes shrink mid-phrase (sheet 06 'it lands', sheet 08 'starts to linger'), tiring to read
Sheet 04: the big chalk title collapses into a small yellow header; the header style then switches between chalk-yellow headlines and white captions that often say the same thing, splitting attention
Sheets 11-12: the 30 s timer bubble sits on top of the burette scale numbers and 'must last 30 s' collides with the stopcock; the timer counts 30 s in about 2.5 s with no cue that time is compressed
Sheets 02-03: tiny labels (NaOH (base), acid + phenolphthalein) fade in at near-unreadable size and then vanish at sheet 04, wasting the setup moment
Sheet 13: the 22.40 mL reading is the strongest frame but arrives at the very end with no hold or emphasis on the meniscus, and the clip ends abruptly
